Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 30-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Generative AI and Applications [IT_4451]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                You are a research engineer developing a generative AI prototype to create short music snippets       (5)  
  based on text prompts (e.g., "generate a calm piano tune"). The team is unsure which model  
  A)           architecture to begin with.  
  Construct a plan to design this generative AI system by specifying:  
  
  1. The type of data and model architecture to use (RNN, Transformer, or GAN-based).  
  2. The training approach (supervised, unsupervised, or hybrid).  
  
  The evaluation metric(s) suitable for generated outputs.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                                                                                                                 (3)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           In your own words, briefly explain and provide examples of how Generative Pre-trained                 (2)  
  Transformers (GPT) are being utilized across three distinct professional fields, such as software  
  development, creative writing, or customer service.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
2)                Explain the different types of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) based on input-output cardinality     (5)  
  (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, and many-to-many) with suitable real-world examples for  
  A)           each. Discuss how these architectures differ in handling sequential data and where each type is  
  best applied.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)           You are designing a language translation model for an Indian startup that aims to translate English   (3)  
  text into French. The team suggests using an RNN-based approach, but you propose using a  
  Transformer model instead.  
  
  Page #1

Apply your understanding of the Transformer encoder-decoder architecture to justify your choice  
  over RNN.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Identify the major technological milestones in the evolution of Generative AI from early symbolic      (2)  
  models to modern multimodal systems. Mention key breakthroughs such as VAEs, GANs,  
  Transformers, Diffusion Models, and recent multimodal advancements.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3)        Develop and analyze the mathematical model of a Denoising Autoencoder (DAE). Explain how               (5)  
  noise is introduced to the input data, how the model learns to reconstruct the original data through  
  A)   the encoder and decoder functions, and discuss its role in feature learning and robust  
  representation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                                                                                                          (3)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Describe the concept of Autoregressive Generation in GPT models and mention any two real-world (2)  
  applications where GPT is commonly used.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Remember"  
  
4)        Apply your understanding to develop an explanation of how pretraining and fine-tuning stages build (5)  
  and enhance large language models' effectiveness. Use examples to illustrate how pretraining  
  A)   large-scale data develops general linguistic knowledge and how fine-tuning adapts the model to  
  specific tasks such as question answering or summarization.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   Construct and analyze the working principle of Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). Explain their          (3)  
  mathematical formulation involving the encoder, decoder, and latent variable learning, and discuss  
  how VAEs differ from traditional autoencoders in generating new data samples.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Interpret how the use of real-world datasets can lead to privacy and security concerns in large        (2)  
  language model training.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5)        Construct and analyze the architecture of a Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network (BiRNN).            (5)  
  Explain how processing sequences in both forward and backward directions improves context  
  A)   understanding and discuss its advantages over a standard RNN with suitable examples.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   While designing a Transformer-based language generator, your model begins producing                    (3)  
  grammatically incorrect sentences because it is using information from words that haven't been  
  generated yet.  
  Apply your understanding of the masked self-attention mechanism to explain how it prevents the  
  Page #2

model from accessing future tokens during decoding.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)               Describe the main purpose of an LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) network and explain how it           (2)  
  overcomes the limitations of a traditional RNN.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Remember"  
  
  
  -----End-----
